verify.note: One archive recording of the first level block, from a cut in play. Each of the five hooks against the original from one state: every register with R, all game memory; after each tile pass the tile layer against the painted map for the hidden screen's 640 cells and Layer 2 against the painted panel; every fourth frame's tiles against the visible screen. The steady-speed build's hooks on the first 3,000 frames; unit cases; 6 broken builds. Blocks 1, 2 and 10 from their own snapshots: games/gauntlet.md.

status.title: Gauntlet
status.build: gauntlet_p1_sprites.nex f33ade47 (nothing of the game changes: each 8 x 8 cell of the play window shown as a painted tile of the tile layer, the status panel painted on Layer 2; the original's pace) + steady 545fdeed (the game at 28 MHz, an update every 3 frames: the original takes 3 to 8); the whole game from the tape: record gauntlet_tape
status.software: Verify IDENTICAL on the first block's recording, 15,698 frames, 3,202 updates (R compared): 2,459,136 cells against the painted map, Layer 2 against the painted panel after every pass; the steady build's hooks IDENTICAL on 3,000 frames; unit PASS (28 cases); 6 of 6 broken builds detected; ROM path check pass; the hooks take 0.016% of the recording's time less than the copies and the clear they stand for. Blocks 1, 2 and 10 from the tape prompt PASSED the same way
status.hardware: untested (both builds start and run in OverSpec)
status.next: the owner's review of the painting and of the steady speed; the heroes' shots (drawn at pixel positions) are not painted; hardware test

techniques.target: the game's hidden screen, its copies and the screen itself unchanged; a painted tile of the tile layer over each cell the map knows, the panel's cells on Layer 2
one window a copy (three an update), the tile pass inside the first; the clear's saved time added to the first copy's target; the window's clock read every row of the pass
HLIB_R_IN / hlib_r_set in the three copy wrappers; an inline form in the clear's hook and the wait's, where nothing may be mapped or no register is free
HLIB_SPEED_IN / OUT in the copy wrappers; the clear's hook writes the speed directly (the original's pace build only)

pacing.coverage: Four whole recordings of blocks 1, 2 and 10 (61,548 frames), the frames an update takes in four more; the copies' and the clear's own times read off the verifier's run of the routines (35,796 + 10,587 + 53,684 T, 34,357 T: the same every time); hook time on the simulator's line clock. No JNext or hardware timing.
pacing.result: An update takes 3 to 8 frames in the original. The copies and the clear run at 28 MHz and their own time is waited out; the tile pass spends part of it. The hooks take 0.016% of a recording's time less than the code they stand for.

dependencies.coverage: Every writer of the screen and of the hidden copy in the first 4,000 frames of block 1 (scan --writers); the interrupt handler over the whole recording (isr); the four plotters, the three copies, the clear; the distinct cells of all 31 block recordings.
dependencies.result: No game code is changed beyond five CALL targets; nothing reads the Next's layers. The handler reads the ROM, so the one hook that runs with interrupts on maps nothing. Bank 7 is never paged by the game (paging locked): the tile layer lives there.

feasibility.decision: Everything painted on the tile layer, looked up from the finished hidden screen at the game's own copy (owner 2026-11-19: 'Go ahead with you recommendation'); the panel on Layer 2 (owner: 'Can you fix up the hud?'); a steady-speed build beside the original's pace (owner: the slowdown 'might be an opportunity to fix that').
feasibility.next_experiment: The tape's level blocks from memory: the loader call answered from pages, proven by a recording that loads a second block; success = the same level data bytes as the tape's block, compared in the verifier.
